name: Atlas SLV-3D Centaur
best_known_for: 1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — paired the Atlas SLV-3D booster with the high-energy Centaur D-1A upper stage to send Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, and Pioneer Venus to deep space
credit: Stretched Atlas booster (the 'Atlas SLV-3D') with the LOX/LH₂ Centaur D-1A — the world's first hydrogen-fuelled upper stage, and the key enabler of every American Jupiter / Saturn / Helios / Mariner mission of the 1970s. Replaced the earlier SLV-3C in 1973, served through 1983 (last flight Intelsat V F-7), and was itself superseded by the Atlas G/H/I family that fed into the Atlas II of the 1990s. The Star-37E or Star-48 solid-kick stage was bolted on top for the very-high-energy trajectories that sent Pioneer 11 past Jupiter to a Saturn rendezvous.
